catalog.title: Website
catalog.summary: An open website brief: the model invents the subject, brand, content and visual direction of a complete site.
catalog.requirement: Original concept and identity; substantial real content; responsive layout; working interactions; accessible and fast

catalog.title: SaaS for Clearing Agents
catalog.summary: A working SaaS product for customs clearing and freight forwarding, with real domain logic rather than generic CRUD.
catalog.requirement: Working product end to end; three or more connected workflows; domain-specific calculations; persistence; import/export; tests for core logic

catalog.title: 2D Game
catalog.summary: A complete 2D game in a single HTML file, with the genre and art direction chosen by the model.
catalog.requirement: Complete game loop; played and taught without a manual; reliable collision and timing; feedback and sound; keyboard and touch controls

catalog.title: 3D Game
catalog.summary: A complete 3D game in a single HTML file, with the genre, world and camera model chosen by the model.
catalog.requirement: Genuine 3D play; authored environment; working objective and progression; reliable controls and camera; stable frame rate

catalog.title: Restaurant Website
catalog.summary: A restaurant or cafe website with a full menu, reservations and a distinctive art direction.
catalog.requirement: Real menu with 30+ items; reservation and order flows with validation; opening-hours logic; strong identity; responsive and accessible

catalog.title: Machine Explainer
catalog.summary: An interactive visual explainer of a real machine or physical system that is accurate enough for an engineer.
catalog.requirement: One source of truth for state; timeline scrubbing; part inspection with accurate explanations; two or more live readouts; what-if simulation

catalog.title: First-Person Game
catalog.summary: A complete first-person 3D game with pointer-lock movement, an authored environment and reactive gameplay.
catalog.requirement: Pointer-lock movement with real collision; animated view-model; authored environment; reactive opponents or hazards; complete loop; saved progress

catalog.title: Arcade Game
catalog.summary: A score-attack arcade game designed around one more run, with seeded runs and a local leaderboard.
catalog.requirement: Scoring with real risk and reward; escalation beyond speed; modifiers with trade-offs; seeded and daily runs; ghost or replay; juice and generative audio

catalog.title: Browser Operating System
catalog.summary: A complete desktop operating system in the browser with its own identity, window management and a shared filesystem.
catalog.requirement: Window manager with snap and z-order; persisted shared filesystem; eight or more apps including a terminal and editor; launcher search; persistent settings

catalog.title: Rubik's Cube
catalog.summary: A physically convincing 3D Rubik's Cube with direct manipulation, a speedcubing timer and a solver that actually solves any scramble.
catalog.requirement: Correct cubie state as source of truth; drag-to-turn and full notation; scramble, undo and redo; timer with ao5 and ao12; solver that animates any scramble

catalog.title: Platformer
catalog.summary: An original 2D platformer with one mechanic twist of the model's invention, four levels and a boss.
catalog.requirement: Excellent movement with coyote time and input buffering; solid tile collision; four escalating levels; distinct enemies and a boss; level select with saved progress

catalog.title: Living 3D World
catalog.summary: An explorable 3D world that feels inhabited: streaming terrain, weather and time systems, creatures with routines.
catalog.requirement: Seamless exploration with collision; seeded procedural streaming world; weather and time that change gameplay; believable inhabitants; save/load and map

catalog.title: Data Story
catalog.summary: An interactive data-driven story built on a generated dataset, told through linked custom visualisations.
catalog.requirement: Four or more hand-built visual forms with linked interaction; a genuine insight with a narrative arc; annotations, tooltips and CSV export; responsive redraw

catalog.title: Generative Art
catalog.summary: A seeded generative artwork that evolves in real time and is worth watching rather than a screensaver.
catalog.requirement: Deterministic seeding from the URL; three or more scenes or developments; collaborative interaction; high-resolution PNG export; adaptive resolution

catalog.title: Music Instrument
catalog.summary: A browser instrument or mini-workstation that sounds genuinely good, built on a real Web Audio engine.
catalog.requirement: Real sound engine with envelopes, filters and effects; sequencer with tempo and swing; presets, save/load and WAV export; live visualisation

catalog.title: Creative Tool
catalog.summary: A professional-grade creative tool in the browser: layered, non-destructive, fast and dense enough for real work.
catalog.requirement: Real file open and export; layered non-destructive workflow with undo/redo; eight or more tools; autosave; smooth zoom and pan on large canvases

catalog.title: Emergent Simulation
catalog.summary: A simulation sandbox where simple rules produce rich, surprising behaviour that rewards watching.
catalog.requirement: Deterministic fixed-timestep simulation with three or more interacting systems; thousands of entities at 60 FPS; inspection tools and live graphs; presets and save/load

catalog.title: Strategy Game
catalog.summary: An original strategy or tactics game won by thinking, against an AI opponent built on real search or evaluation.
catalog.requirement: Clean rules engine with legal-move validation; AI with multiple difficulties using real techniques; three or more scenarios; tutorial; save/load

catalog.title: Spreadsheet
catalog.summary: A real spreadsheet application with a formula engine, a virtualised grid and charting.
catalog.requirement: Formula parser without eval with 40+ functions and cycle detection; 100k-row virtualised grid; copy/paste interchange; three chart types; CSV import and export

catalog.title: Physics Engine
catalog.summary: A 2D rigid-body physics engine written from scratch, with a delightful sandbox built on top of it.
catalog.requirement: Circles and convex polygons with SAT or GJK; friction, restitution and joints; stable stacks; fixed timestep; 500+ bodies; debug overlay and scene save/load

catalog.title: Floating Pagoda Island
catalog.summary: A fixed brief: an explorable floating island crowned by a multi-tier pagoda, built entirely in code.
catalog.requirement: Procedural pagoda with real construction detail; island geology; waterfalls and cloud sea; day cycle with lantern light; exploration and interaction

runs.notes: A self-contained canvas arcade flight game with procedural night-garden art, synthesized sound, escalating hazard density, pulse ability, keyboard/pointer/touch input, pause, and locally saved best score. Runs without external assets; browser storage and audio may be restricted by privacy settings.

Single-file 2D twin-stick gravity-well survival game (VORTEX). Vector-drawn canvas art, Web Audio synthesized SFX and music, particles, screen shake, hit-stop, slow-mo, dash, combo scoring, escalating endless waves, persistent best score via guarded localStorage. Known limitations: no external assets; touch and gamepad bindings implemented but not hardware-verified.

LUMENFALL is a complete single-file canvas action game: a lantern spirit survives escalating waves of crystalline enemies, collecting motes of light, chaining combos, dashing through danger and unleashing a screen-clearing Nova. All art is drawn procedurally on canvas and all music and sound effects are synthesized with Web Audio. Includes title, pause, game-over and restart flows, persistent high score, mouse and keyboard controls, and touch controls. Known limitation: the game is tuned for desktop and landscape play; touch firing is automatic and the arena is best experienced on a wider screen.

Aether Drift: neon top-down arena shooter/collector with waves, boss every 5th wave, phase (slow-mo+invuln) mechanic, entropy discharge via cores, procedural canvas art, synth audio+music, touch/gamepad support. Known limitations: music loop simple; no explicit victory state (endless survival).

ClearDesk: a client-side SaaS for customs clearing agents covering job lifecycle, customs entry duty/VAT calculation, demurrage, charges/invoicing, and document generation. Monochrome UI, localStorage persistence with try/catch, seeded demo data, tests for core logic. No server or build required.
A self-contained monochrome editorial field guide to the city after closing, with procedural canvas artwork, responsive layouts, and interactive field notes. No external assets or dependencies.

NOCTURNE — a monochrome single-page atlas of the night train. Twelve real sleeper services (1883 to today) presented as a split-flap departures board, a hand-drawn Beck-style route diagram, per-service night sequences, and four short elegies. Static HTML/CSS/JS with no dependencies and no external requests; the split-flap engine is DOM + Web Animations, board clacks are synthesized with the Web Audio API (off by default), the diagram is hand-authored SVG. Fully responsive, keyboard accessible, motion respects prefers-reduced-motion, works from file:// and GitHub Pages subpaths. Known limitations: timetable times are indicative rather than authoritative (stated on the page) and the diagram is deliberately schematic, not to scale.

Single-page monochrome interactive experience 'DIM — The Hour Between': scroll narrative on dusk and the hour between day and night, with a functional light-level dial, star/fog sky layers and a keeper's log. Hand-written HTML/CSS/vanilla JS and local SVG; no framework, no build step, no external assets. Known limitations: no-JS fallback leaves scroll-reveal content hidden until JavaScript runs; imagery is CSS/SVG only.

Umbra is a single-page exhibition of twelve generative monochrome studies drawn live on Canvas 2D: interference rings, a halftone field, a flow field, ordered Bayer dithering, a harmonograph, phyllotaxis, marching-squares contours, Rule 30, stacked sine scans, a typographic density field, moire gratings and a halftoned sphere. Each plate is seeded and has two live parameters, a deep link, a PNG export and a pointer luminance readout; the method section adds an interactive tone-quantisation demo. Zero dependencies, no webfonts, no image files, no build step, relative paths throughout. Motion is capped at 30 fps, pauses off-screen and in hidden tabs, and defaults to paused under prefers-reduced-motion. Verified in Chromium at 1000x700: no console errors, only local asset requests, and every control, dialog, keyboard path and hash deep link exercised. The test browser could not produce animation frames (no visible window), so the twelve renderers were additionally run against a software rasteriser to confirm output and coverage, and responsive breakpoints were reviewed in CSS rather than emulated; Firefox and Safari were not available.

A complete monochrome fictional institution, the Bureau of Unseen Places. The site combines an editorial introduction, a live procedural survey-plate generator with four landforms and two atmospheric controls, a collected archive with accessible detail dialogs, SVG downloads, responsive layouts, and reduced-motion support. All artwork is generated inline in the browser; there are no external assets or dependencies. Known limitations: system fonts vary slightly between operating systems, and JavaScript is required for the plate generator and archive.

Gnomon: a single self-contained index.html (inline CSS and JS, no external assets, no dependencies) about sundials. It has a hero whose title casts a long shadow from a movable light, a working horizontal sundial driven by latitude and solar time, and an analemma driven by an approximate equation-of-time model. Everything is monochrome and drawn with CSS and SVG. Limitations: the page was syntax-checked and statically checked for colour, but not opened in a real browser, so layout and performance on devices are untested. Live solar time uses the time zone's standard meridian rather than the viewer's exact longitude, and the equation of time is a low-order approximation, so readings can be off by several minutes. The shadow on the dial has a fixed length and is drawn only between 06:00 and 18:00 apparent solar time.

Two Tones is a single-file, strictly greyscale interactive atlas of dithering. It renders procedural sphere, ramp and relief sources on canvas through four 1-bit methods (threshold, Bayer ordered, Floyd–Steinberg, Atkinson), and includes a live studio, a pointer-driven hero light, an orbit toggle, PNG export, scroll progress and reduced-motion support. It uses no external files, fonts or libraries. Limitation: verified with static checks and a stubbed-DOM run only, not in a real browser, so visual layout and motion are untested; browsers without :has() show the selected-state styling less clearly.

Single-page monochrome interactive experience 'GRAVITY': generative canvas particle fields, scroll-driven reveals, an interactive gravity-well demo, and a dark/light monochrome theme toggle. Static HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, relative paths. Known limitations: external Google Fonts dependency for typography; canvas animations disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

Standalone monochrome customs-clearance operations desk with local demo authentication, persistent declaration CRUD, search and filters, guarded status progression, indicative ZAR duty/VAT calculations, CSV export and printable text documents. No server or third-party integration; accounts and operational data are browser-local, and customs calculations are estimates requiring verification.

ClearDesk — a working SaaS for customs clearing agents: full clearance-entry pipeline with guarded status transitions (new → awaiting docs → lodged → customs query → assessed → duty paid → released → delivered → closed), an HS tariff schedule, duty/excise/VAT computation with pro-rata CIF allocation and FX conversion, per-mode document checklists that gate lodging, a disbursement ledger with aging buckets and payments, client statements, dashboard KPIs/reports, global search, keyboard shortcuts, CSV exports and printable duty-computation/entry sheets. Pure static product: index.html runs directly from file:// or any static host with zero install; data persists in localStorage (every access wrapped in try/catch with an in-memory fallback and warning banner). Auth is local (salted SHA-256), seed data is generated relative to the current date, and the domain-logic test suite can be run from Settings → Diagnostics (also 'node assets/core.test.js'). Demo credentials are shown on the sign-in screen: clara.otien@atlasfreight.app / demo1234 (manager) and james.mwangi@atlasfreight.app / demo1234 (clerk). Known limitations: single-browser storage, illustrative tariff rates, no real customs-authority or payment integration, local-only auth.

ClearLane is a client-side SaaS prototype for customs clearing agents: shipment CRUD with domain validation, customs value and duty/tax calculations, document generation (commercial invoice, packing list, customs entry export) and a clearance status workflow. Ships as a static build with localStorage persistence and seeded demo data. Known limitations: no server-side backend or real auth provider, demo-grade password hashing, illustrative duty rate table only, no live customs API integration.

Clearway is a local-first customs clearance desk for clearing agents: job files, client records, live duty/MPF/HMF estimates, document control, status workflow, entry worksheets, printable entry summaries, CSV exports, and dashboard/report analytics. It runs with no server, build step, API keys, or external accounts; state persists in localStorage and is seeded with a 14-job demo workspace (ops@clearway.co / clearway123). Known limitations: browser-local data only with no sync or server-side auth; passwords are salted and hashed locally but this is not an enterprise identity system; duty/MPF/HMF figures are seeded operational estimates, not a live tariff database or legal filing; document attachments are not stored, only document metadata and references; no customs authority or broker network integration.

Declarant is a local-first customs clearing workspace for a Mombasa freight desk. It covers intake, document checklists with lodgement gates, pro-rata CIF allocation, duty/excise/VAT/levy computation, assessments, customs queries, release and delivery, disbursement aging, client statements, CSV exports, print documents and role-based demo accounts. Runs directly from index.html with seeded data and localStorage persistence; no server, build step or external services. Limitations: tariff rates and the demo accounts are illustrative and not a substitute for current authority tariffs or real authentication; data is confined to one browser profile; CSV and print output are the only integrations; the bundled test suite covers core calculations, document gating, aging and storage serialisation, not browser rendering.
